title: Why isn't the answer 0?
text: A zero exponent does not mean the base is multiplied by zero. $$\frac{7^{3}}{7^{3}} = 7^{3-3} = 7^{0}$$, and any nonzero number divided by itself is 1. A common mistake is to answer 0. What exponent is left when you compute $$3 - 3$$?

title: What value matches that quotient?
text: $$7^{3} \div 7^{3}$$ equals 1, and that quotient is $$7^{0}$$. What is $$343 \div 343$$?

title: Worked solution
text: $$7^{0} = 1$$. Common mistake: answering 0. General rule: any nonzero number raised to the power 0 equals 1. The reason is that subtracting exponents in a quotient of equal powers leaves exponent 0 and value 1.
